newsitem.title: BELGIUM: No EU plans to make D. Telekom sell cable network.
newsitem.headline: No EU plans to make D. Telekom sell cable network.

text.p: The European Commission has no plans to present proposals in March to force Deutsche Telekom to sell part or all of its cable television network, a European Commission source said on Wednesday.

But the Commission, under the direction of Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert, had ordered an independent study on the link between cable television and telecommunications networks, the source said.

A report released on Tuesday ahead of publication in the latest issue of the German monthly magazine Capital said Deutsche Telekom was so worried about the Commission's findings that chief executive Ron Sommer planned to meet behind closed doors with the German parliament's postal affairs committee.
The source said the Commission had to complete an analysis before January 1, 1998, as required by EU directives on cable networks and the deregulation of telecommunications.
The study was under way but the Commission had not yet received any intermediate reports, the source said.
He also said the study did not look at any particular country or company, but at the whole of the EU.
Van Miert has in the past taken a critical view of Deutsche Telekom's ownership of Germany's only cable television network.
Capital said Van Miert was studying three alternative proposals to weaken Telekom's control of the cable TV market, but the Commission source said there had been no mention of this.
They are to force Telekom to divest its network completely, put it into a separate company or break it up into regional cable companies. -- Brussels newsroom +32 2 287 68 11
